result.title: RespFocus: Learning Temporal Evidence for Weakly Supervised Respiratory Sound Classification
result.summary: Respiratory auscultation provides a low-cost means of assessing pulmonary function, yet transient crackles and sustained wheezes can be difficult to recognize in noisy clinical recordings. Conventional deep learning classifiers often operate as black boxes, offering limited insight into the temporal acoustic evidence supporting their predictions. We present RespFocus, a weakly supervised framework that uses multiple instance learning (MIL) to learn inspectable temporal evidence from cycle-level labels and integrate it into classification. We also introduce PedResp2026, a multicenter pediatric respiratory sound cohort collected in routine clinical environments with adjudicated cycle-level annotations. In classification experiments, RespFocus achieves four-class Scores of 69.55\% on public ICBHI 2017 and 72.91\% on PedResp2026. Evidence diagnostics and matched temporal interventions support the functional contribution of the learned evidence to model predictions. Together, these findings highlight RespFocus's potential as a tool for automated respiratory sound diagnosis.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 RespFocus，用多实例学习从周期级弱标签中学习可检查的时间声学证据并将其融入呼吸音四分类，同时构建多中心儿科呼吸音数据集 PedResp2026，并报告了证据诊断与匹配时间干预实验。
AI.relevance_reason: 其 MIL 式证据定位与「matched temporal interventions」对所学证据功能贡献的检验，可能为 LVR 中 latent 视觉证据筛选、证据使用与贡献分配提供可核查的方法线索；但研究对象是音频弱监督分类，能否迁移到多模态潜在推理状态仍需阅读原文判断。
